## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pattasannicaya* ("The training rule on collecting almsbowls") is the opening rule of the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* (relinquishment with confession) section in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule regulates the possession of almsbowls among nuns, providing that a nun who keeps or accumulates more than one bowl must relinquish the surplus bowl and confess the transgression. An English translation of the text has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Curated parallels for this rule exist in the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (*Np* 1) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (*Np* 1), as well as across the monastic codes of other early Buddhist schools. Corresponding rules on bowl accumulation are preserved in the Chinese versions of the Dharmaguptaka (*Np* 24), Mahīśāsaka (*Np* 30), Sarvāstivāda (*Np* 19), Mūlasarvāstivāda (*Np* 20), and Mahāsāṅghika (*Np* 14) traditions, in the Sanskrit Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅga* (*Np* 14), and in the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda tradition (*Np* 20).

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
